source.title: Towards LLM Unlearning Resilient to Relearning Attacks: A Sharpness-Aware Minimization Perspective and Beyond
source.authors: Chong-Yu Fan; Jing-Han Jia; Yihua Zhang; Anil Ramakrishna; Ming-Yi Hong; Si-Jia Liu

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses the shallow-alignment issue to motivate a smoothness-based unlearning defense and reports how that defense performs. Its experiments concern unlearning and recovery of forgotten knowledge, not the claim versions' safety-training and refusal behavior.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on relearning and jailbreaking after unlearning, plus token-wise KL between an unlearned model and its original model. These are related to the claim but do not measure safety-trained versus base models, refusal rates after initial fine-tuning, or the claim's aligned-versus-base KL. No result qualifies as a row for V1–V7; related findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: This is an LLM unlearning robustness paper built on NPO, SAM and other smoothing methods, tested on WMDP and MUSE. It cites shallow safety alignment (Qi et al.) only as an analogy for its own 'shallow unlearning alignment' observation. That observation is token-wise KL between an unlearned model and its pre-unlearning original under GCG prompts. No result measures harmful-request compliance or refusal of a safety-trained model, or aligned-versus-base KL. Relearning restores suppressed knowledge (multiple-choice accuracy), not safety refusal. No version is tested. The record's 'uses_without_test/T4' overstates the link: the paper does not rely on the finding as a tool, it only invokes it to interpret Fig. 6(b).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that smoothness optimization, especially SAM, makes LLM unlearning more robust to relearning and to input-level jailbreaking attacks. They read the small early-token KL for NPO as 'shallow unlearning alignment', analogous to shallow safety alignment, and say smoothing alleviates it.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies SAM and other smoothness methods to machine unlearning and evaluates recovery of forgotten knowledge and unlearning under jailbreaking; it does not use the safety fine-tuning or aligned-versus-base KL recipes in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The effects vary with relearning sample count and epoch count, the smoothness method, and SAM perturbation radius. The paper reports that too-small ρ gives limited robustness improvement and too-large ρ disrupts forgetting.

fits_no_version.finding: Relearning an NPO-unlearned Zephyr-7B-beta on 20/40/60 WMDP Bio forget samples for one epoch drops UE from 0.74 to 0.57/0.39/0.37. SAM keeps it at 0.70/0.50/0.45.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small-data fine-tuning restores knowledge suppressed by LLM unlearning; smoothness optimization resists this.

fits_no_version.finding: Under GCG prompts, NPO loses UE while NPO+SAM and NPO+RS are described as lossless. NPO's token-wise KL from the original model is small at the first few output tokens; smoothed variants raise it there.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning is concentrated away from early output tokens ('shallow unlearning'), and this enables input-level recovery attacks.

record.problems: The relevant token-wise KL and jailbreaking outcomes are presented in figures without numeric values in the text. Relearning attack performance is averaged over five random trials, but no error bars or other uncertainty estimates are stated in the provided text. The experiments concern unlearning rather than safety-training-induced refusal behavior.
record.rows_left_out: No additional WMDP or MUSE relearning-table results were extracted because they measure recovery of unlearned knowledge, not any claim version's safety-refusal behavior. Fig. 6(a) includes other smoothness variants, but the text does not separately characterize their jailbreaking outcomes; the plot values are figure-only.

untested.parts: No harmful fine-tuning of a safety-trained model and no compliance/refusal measure. Relearning starts from unlearned models and measures WMDP accuracy.
Relearning on AGNews, GSM8K and SST2 (Fig. 4) is benign data, but it measures recovery of unlearned knowledge, not harmful compliance of a safety-aligned model.
Per-token KL is computed between unlearned and original models, not aligned and base models.
GCG prefixes are used to recover unlearned knowledge, not to bypass refusal. No prefill or decoding attacks.
The RMU layer-subset/perturbed-parameter analysis (Fig. A2) concerns unlearning robustness, not localization of safety behaviour.
Smoothness methods deepen unlearning across tokens, not safety alignment. Durability of safety deepening is not tested.

record.verdict_notes: Relation/tranche changed from uses_without_test/T4 to discusses/T6, because the shallow-alignment paper is cited only as an interpretive analogy. All rows correctly carry versions ['none']. The Fig. 6(b) KL pattern is the nearest analogue to V3, but it concerns unlearned-versus-original divergence, not aligned-versus-base divergence.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test initial harmful fine-tuning of a safety-trained model or measure refusal/compliance rates; relearning starts from an already-unlearned model.
Does not fine-tune on ordinary or carefully selected benign instruction data or measure harmful compliance.
Measures token-wise KL between unlearned and original models, not aligned and base models.
Tests enhanced-GCG adversarial prefixes against unlearned models, but not compliant-opening prefills, suffixes or decoding changes against safety-trained refusal behavior.
Does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Does not test whether safety-training data or objectives produce shallow safety alignment.
Smoothness methods are applied to unlearning, not to training that deepens safety alignment; durability of deeper safety alignment is not tested.

rows.measure: UE (1 − WMDP Bio evaluation accuracy; higher indicates better unlearning)
rows.locator: Fig. 1(a) and motivating example in Sec. 3
rows.note: The paper describes recovery of harmful responses after relearning. This is recovery from an already-unlearned model, not initial safety fine-tuning or a refusal-rate measure.
